_doc: Map: figure number (or 'appendix-N') → print asset, resolved against the search path paper/figures/ then data/analysis/figures/ (first match wins). After pandoc renders the .docx, paper/build.py rewrites each to point at the resolved asset so the final PDF ships the in-repo figure (current at HEAD) instead of whatever bitmap the .docx embedded. format=svg → vector, no DPI check; format=png → min_dpi enforced via Pillow. format=pdf is ALWAYS rejected: WeasyPrint has no PDF image decoder and would emit a silently blank figure — convert to SVG with `pdftocairo -svg` into paper/figures/ instead. Set 'optional': true on entries with no canonical asset yet (build warns and keeps the .docx bitmap rather than erroring).
_numbering: Numbering tracks '2026 Anthropic Surfaceome Technical Draft (4).docx' (7 main figures). Earlier manifest revisions numbered a 2-figure draft; re-check these keys against the caption order whenever the .docx figure set changes, because the swap keys purely off the figure-N anchor that filters/figures.lua derives from the caption.

1.description: Five-way Venn of the source surface-protein databases; 188-protein core. Vector, converted from db_overlap_venn.pdf (the canonical PNG carries no DPI tEXt chunk, so it cannot pass the min_dpi gate). max_width preserves the author's sizing: this figure was 3.96in in the .docx and is nearly square, so unlike the wide panel figures it towers over the page if allowed to fill the full column-span width.

2.description: SurfaceBench classification accuracy: triage agent vs the five source databases. Vector, converted from db_correctness_by_class.pdf.

3.description: Zero-DB rescues grouped by agent rationale (yes / contextual panels). Vector, converted from zero_db_rescues_by_triage.pdf.

4.description: Three-stage deep-dive pipeline schematic (Illustrator-exported, natively vector).

5.description: Five-tier confidence spectrum + positive-call composition. Vector, converted from deep_dive_final_categories.pdf.

6.description: Five-panel violin of record richness by confidence tier. Deliberately raster, NOT vector: the per-gene dots (n = 5,130 × 5 panels) make the SVG ~20 MB and slow to render, while the 600-DPI PNG is 14,659 px wide — far above print need.

7.description: Two-panel viewer composite (a: homepage table with the CD81 row, b: SRC detail page). Inherently a screenshot, so the SVG legitimately wraps two base64 rasters (2749x1212 and 2644x1078) — hence allow_embedded_raster. Still a large upgrade on the .docx bitmap, which was a single 780x666 px flatten shown at 6.5in (~120 DPI, visibly soft). Do not be fooled by the aspect-ratio mismatch against the .docx bitmap: the SVG has different whitespace padding around the panels, not different content.

4.description: Raster on purpose: curator_vs_agent_reason.pdf converts to an SVG that only wraps a raster panel, so the 600-DPI PNG is the sharper asset.

9.description: Raster on purpose: topology_coverage_by_source.pdf converts to an SVG that only wraps a raster panel, so the 600-DPI PNG is the sharper asset.

11.description: Raster on purpose: the vector conversion is 4.1 MB (a dense per-paper scatter), against a 600-DPI PNG 6,997 px wide.

13.description: Raster on purpose: triage_vs_deep_dive_reason.pdf converts to an SVG that only wraps a raster panel, so the 600-DPI PNG is the sharper asset.

_supplementary_note: Supplementary figures were shipping as the .docx's 2048px Google-Docs exports while 600-DPI / vector canonical renders existed for all 14 — the visible resolution gap against the main figures. Slugs resolved from each caption's gist id via data/analysis/figures/gist_map.json, so the mapping is the manuscript's own, not inferred from titles.
